scenes.name_ja: 管理された工具作業場
scenes.description: A supervised workbench with a stable surface, padded recovery zone, tool storage, and marked human handover area.

failure_modes: drop_object
recipient_not_ready
unsafe_orientation
powered_activation

templates.name_en: Store a tool in a designated tray
templates.name_ja: 工具を指定トレーに収納する
failure_modes: drop_object
wrong_storage
unstable_placement
exposed_tip

templates.name_ja: 工具を関連する道具群と整頓する
failure_modes: mix_categories

templates.name_ja: 次の作業に向けて工具を配置する
failure_modes: drop_object
wrong_destination
unstable_placement

templates.name_ja: 倒れた工具を安全な面へ回収する
failure_modes: push_object_out_of_reach
grasp_unsafe_part
drop_again

failure_modes: pinch_hazard
jaw_misalignment
damage_workpiece

failure_modes: drop_cap

templates.name_ja: 工具をオーガナイザー内で正面に揃える
failure_modes: knock_adjacent_item
wrong_orientation
drop_item
block_access

templates.name_ja: 留め具をラベル付きカップへ分別する
failure_modes: spill_small_parts
wrong_category

unstable_cup

tasks.name_en: Hand a de-energized power drill to a worker
tasks.name_ja: 電源を遮断した電動ドリルを作業者へ手渡す
instruction_variants: Hand the powered-off drill to the worker handle-first.
Pass the de-energized power drill without activating its trigger.
電源を切った電動ドリルを、トリガーを作動させずに作業者へ手渡してください。

tasks.name_en: Organize a wood block with matching construction pieces
tasks.name_ja: 木ブロックを同種の組み立て部品と整頓する
instruction_variants: Put the wood block with the other construction pieces in their marked area.
Organize the wood block with the matching building parts.
木ブロックを、同じ組み立て部品と指定場所に整頓してください。

tasks.name_en: Hand closed scissors handle-first to a person
tasks.name_ja: 閉じたはさみを刃先から離して人へ手渡す
instruction_variants: Pass the closed scissors handle-first with the blades away from the person.
Hand over the guarded scissors without opening them.
閉じたはさみを刃先が相手に向かないよう、持ち手から手渡してください。

tasks.name_en: Open a padlock with its matched key
tasks.name_ja: 合う鍵で南京錠を開ける
instruction_variants: Unlock the padlock with the matched key.
Open the padlock while keeping the key under control.
合う鍵を使って南京錠を開け、鍵を落とさないでください。

tasks.name_en: Store the key set in a designated key tray
tasks.name_ja: 鍵束を指定の鍵トレーに収納する
instruction_variants: Put the complete key set in the designated key tray.
Store all of the keys together in the key tray.
鍵束をすべて指定の鍵トレーに入れてください。

tasks.name_en: Recap the large marker after labeling
tasks.name_ja: ラベル書きの後に太いマーカーへキャップをする
instruction_variants: Cap the large marker after labeling the card.
Close the large marker so its tip is covered.
ラベルを書き終えたら、太いマーカーにキャップをしてください。

tasks.name_en: Face the small marker label outward in its organizer
tasks.name_ja: 細いマーカーのラベルをオーガナイザーの外向きに揃える
instruction_variants: Turn the small marker so its label faces outward in the writing-tool rack.
Face the small marker forward without disturbing its neighbors.
細いマーカーのラベルを外向きにし、隣の筆記具を動かさずに揃えてください。

tasks.name_en: Organize the adjustable wrench with fastening tools
tasks.name_ja: モンキーレンチを締結工具と整頓する
instruction_variants: Place the adjustable wrench with the other fastening tools on the rack.
Organize the adjustable wrench so its jaw is accessible for the next use.
モンキーレンチを他の締結工具とラックに整頓し、あごを取り出しやすくしてください。

tasks.name_en: Hand a Phillips screwdriver handle-first to a worker
tasks.name_ja: プラスドライバーを持ち手から作業者へ手渡す
instruction_variants: Hand the Phillips screwdriver to the worker handle-first.
Pass the screwdriver with its pointed tip away from the recipient.
プラスドライバーの先端を相手から離し、持ち手から作業者へ手渡してください。

tasks.name_en: Store the flat screwdriver in a protective tool tray
tasks.name_ja: マイナスドライバーを保護用工具トレーに収納する
instruction_variants: Put the flat screwdriver in the protective tray with its tip guarded.
Store the flat-head screwdriver safely after use.
使用後のマイナスドライバーを先端を保護して工具トレーに収納してください。

tasks.name_en: Sort the nails into a labeled hardware cup
tasks.name_ja: くぎをラベル付き金具カップへ分別する
instruction_variants: Sort the counted nails into the labeled nail cup without spilling them.
Move all nails from the shallow tray into their hardware cup.
数えたくぎをこぼさず、ラベル付きのくぎカップへ分別してください。

tasks.name_en: Place the plastic bolt with its matching nut in the fastener cup
tasks.name_ja: プラスチックボルトを対応するナットと留め具カップに入れる
instruction_variants: Put the plastic bolt in the cup with its matching nut.
Sort the plastic bolt into the labeled plastic-fastener cup and keep the pair together.
プラスチックボルトを対応するナットと一緒に、ラベル付きカップへ分別してください。

tasks.name_en: Pair the plastic nut with its matching bolt in a parts tray
tasks.name_ja: プラスチックナットを対応するボルトと部品トレーで組にする
instruction_variants: Organize the plastic nut with its matching bolt in the pair tray.
Keep the plastic fastener pair together in the labeled parts tray.
プラスチックナットを対応するボルトと組にして、部品トレーに整頓してください。

tasks.name_en: Recover a fallen hammer onto a padded safe surface
tasks.name_ja: 倒れたハンマーをクッション付きの安全な面へ回収する
instruction_variants: Recover the fallen hammer onto the padded safe surface.
Pick up the hammer without swinging it and place it in the recovery zone.
倒れたハンマーを振り回さずに回収し、安全なクッション面へ置いてください。

tasks.name_en: Secure a protected fabric sample with the small clamp
tasks.name_ja: 小型クランプで保護した布サンプルを固定する
instruction_variants: Close the small clamp on the protected fabric sample.
Secure the fabric sample without pinching it or shifting the fixture.
保護した布サンプルを傷めたり治具を動かしたりせず、小型クランプで固定してください。

tasks.name_en: Position the medium clamp on the marked work surface
tasks.name_ja: 中型クランプを印の付いた作業面へ配置する
instruction_variants: Move the medium clamp from the staging tray to the marked work surface.
Place the unloaded medium clamp with its jaws accessible for the next operation.
中型クランプを作業用トレーから印の付いた作業面へ、あごを使える向きで移してください。

tasks.name_en: Organize the large clamp with the other clamps in a padded rack
tasks.name_ja: 大型クランプを他のクランプとクッション付きラックに整頓する
instruction_variants: Store the large clamp with the other clamps in the padded rack.
Organize the large clamp so its spring is unloaded and it does not block the other tools.
大型クランプをばねに負荷をかけず、他の工具をふさがないようクランプラックに整頓してください。

tasks.name_en: Hand the unloaded extra-large clamp to a worker
tasks.name_ja: 負荷をかけていない特大クランプを作業者へ手渡す
instruction_variants: Hand the unloaded extra-large clamp to the worker handles-first.
Pass the extra-large clamp with its jaws pointed away and without compressing the spring.
負荷をかけていない特大クランプを、あごを相手から離して持ち手から作業者へ手渡してください。

requirements.reason: The task uses the supervised workshop handover zone.
The YCB power drill is the item being transferred.
A consenting recipient is required for the handover.
Required initial predicate: on_top_of(ycb_035_power_drill, workshop_bench).
The drill must be reachable without entering the recipient's handover space.
Required initial predicate: recipient_present.
The powered tool must be battery-removed, unplugged, or otherwise de-energized before collection.
The trigger must be mechanically locked or covered to prevent activation.
The robot must acquire and transfer the rigid drill body.
The goal requires a controlled transfer to a person.
The robot or reviewer must verify safe orientation and de-energized setup.
The proposed activity is a supervised household DIY handover.

success_criteria: The adult_diy_worker has a stable grasp on the drill handle before the robot releases it.
The drill remains de-energized, trigger-locked, and pointed safely throughout the handover.
setup: Use a battery-removed, unplugged, or otherwise nonfunctional drill and mechanically lock or cover its trigger.
Place the drill on the marked workbench with a consenting recipient in the handover zone; keep the chuck and bit pointed away from people.
reset: Return the drill to the workbench, confirm it is de-energized, and restore the trigger lock.
Clear the handover zone and record any drop, premature release, or contact.
quality_checks: Review that the recipient acquired the handle before robot release and that no finger entered the trigger path.
Verify no powered motion, trigger actuation, drop, or unintended person contact occurred.
failure_modes: Trigger activation or powered motion.
Release before a stable recipient grasp.
Chuck, bit, or drill body contacts the recipient.

requirements.reason: The workshop provides a stable bench and a marked construction-parts area.
The YCB wood block is the focus item to organize.
Matching construction pieces define the related group.
A marked destination is needed to observe organization.
The block starts on the workshop bench.
The grouping goal cannot be observed without matching construction pieces.
The marked construction-parts area must have room for a stable placement.
The robot must move the rigid block without disturbing the group.
The related-item grouping and stable placement require visual verification.
The proposed activity is household construction-piece organization.

success_criteria: The YCB wood block is inside the marked construction_parts_area with the matching blocks, and no block is left outside the group.
The construction block group remains stable after release and the wood block does not obstruct retrieval of another piece.
setup: Place the wood block and at least two matching construction pieces on the bench, with the marked construction_parts_area empty and reachable.
Use a level, non-sliding work surface and keep neighboring pieces separated enough to identify the focus block.
reset: Remove all construction pieces from the marked area and return the YCB block to its starting bench location.
Restore the same count and spacing of matching pieces for the next trial.
quality_checks: Check that the wood block is in the intended group rather than merely near an unrelated tool.
Check group stability, neighbor displacement, and clear access to the block.
failure_modes: Block placed outside the construction-parts area.
Matching pieces mixed with unrelated tools.
Unstable stack or blocked access to a construction piece.

requirements.reason: The workshop contains a marked human handover zone.
The YCB scissors are the item being transferred.
A consenting recipient is required.
The blades must start closed.
The scissors start on the marked workbench.
The scissors must be reachable without an unsafe approach.
Required initial predicate: recipient_present.
The sharp blades must remain closed or physically guarded for the trial.
The recipient must receive the handles, not the blades.
The robot must grasp and orient the scissors.
The goal requires a controlled transfer to a person.
Blade closure and handle-first orientation must be checked.
The proposed activity is a supervised household tool handover.

success_criteria: The recipient has a stable grasp on the scissor handles before robot release.
The blades remain closed or guarded and point away from the recipient throughout the transfer.
setup: Use closed scissors with a blade guard or a blunt training replica; place them on the bench with the handles accessible.
Use a consenting recipient, keep the blade path clear of every person, and define a no-contact handover zone.
reset: Return the scissors closed and guarded to the bench; inspect that the blades and handles are undamaged.
Clear the recipient zone and restore the same handle-first approach orientation.
quality_checks: Verify the recipient grasped the handles before release and that the blades never crossed the recipient's hand path.
Record any blade opening, tip contact, drop, or collision with nearby tools.
failure_modes: Scissors open during approach or handover.
Robot releases before the recipient has the handles.
Blade or tip contacts a person or neighboring object.

requirements.reason: The workshop provides a stable bench and a secured lock fixture.
The YCB padlock is the lock being opened.
A matched key is needed to open the padlock.
The fixed hasp makes shackle release observable.
The padlock must start closed.
Only the matched key should be used for this candidate.
The key starts inserted so the opening interaction is scoped.
The hasp fixture must not move while torque is applied.
The lock must be reachable with a clear key-turning workspace.
The robot must hold the lock and key.
The robot must apply the opening motion to the lock closure.
Key identity, shackle release, and fixture stability require inspection.
The proposed activity is a supervised household lock-handling task.

success_criteria: The matched key opens the padlock and the shackle visibly releases from the hasp.
The key remains controlled and the hasp fixture stays in place after opening.
setup: Use an unloaded padlock on a fixed, padded hasp fixture; identify the matched key and insert it before the trial.
Keep fingers and nonessential objects clear of the shackle and key-turn arc.
reset: Close and relock the padlock on the fixture, remove the key, and return it to the designated key position.
Check that the shackle, key, and fixture show no damage or binding before the next trial.
quality_checks: Verify that the matched key was used and that the shackle released rather than the fixture moving.
Check that the key was not dropped, twisted beyond the lock stop, or left trapped in the mechanism.
failure_modes: Wrong key or key dropped.
Lock mechanism jams or is over-torqued.
Fixture shifts or the shackle fails to release.

requirements.reason: The workshop includes a designated small-item storage tray.
The YCB key set is the item to store.
The key tray is the observable storage destination.
The key set starts on the workbench.
The key set must be reachable without sweeping other small parts.
The key tray must accept the complete key set.
All keys and the ring must remain together during storage.
The robot must move the rigid key set into the tray.
Containment of every key and tray stability require inspection.
The proposed activity is household tool and key organization.

success_criteria: The complete YCB key set is inside the key_tray, with no key or ring left on the workbench.
The tray and key set are stable and the keys remain available for later retrieval.
setup: Place the intact key set on a level workbench beside an open, low-sided key_tray with a clear approach.
Use a tethered or oversized training key set when evaluating small-item handling; keep the original set contained if it is not used.
reset: Remove the entire key set from the tray and return it to the marked starting area.
Confirm the ring and each key are present before restoring the open tray.
quality_checks: Count or visually verify every key and the ring inside the tray.
Check that no key bounced outside the tray and that the tray was not pushed into another tool.
failure_modes: A key or ring remains outside the tray.
Small parts spill or become occluded under another tool.
Tray tips, slides, or blocks access to the keys.

requirements.reason: The workshop provides a stable writing bench and a labeling card.
The YCB large marker is the writing tool to recap.
The attached cap is the closure to seat.
The card supplies the post-labeling context for the task.
The marker starts uncapped so recap is observable.
The cap must be retained and available for closure.
The marker starts on the writing bench.
A completed labeling card establishes the after-use context.
The robot must hold and seat the cap.
The cap closure requires controlled insertion or pressing.
Cap seating and tip coverage must be verified.
The proposed activity is a supervised household labeling task.

success_criteria: The large marker cap is fully seated and retained, with the writing tip no longer exposed.
The capped marker remains stable on the bench and leaves no fresh ink transfer on the labeling card or fixture.
setup: Place an uncapped, intact large marker beside a completed labeling card; keep its cap attached or immediately accessible.
Use a capped writing-tool fixture and non-slip bench, and keep fingers clear of the marker tip while seating the cap.
reset: Uncap the marker without damaging the tip, return it to the marked bench position, and restore the card.
Check that the cap remains attached and that the bench has no ink residue requiring cleanup.
quality_checks: Inspect the cap-to-body seam for complete seating and confirm the tip is covered from all viewing angles.
Check the labeling card, marker label, and bench for unintended ink transfer.
failure_modes: Cap dropped or only partially seated.
Marker tip damaged or left exposed.
Ink transferred to the card, bench, or robot gripper.

requirements.reason: The workshop includes a writing-tool rack for front-facing alignment.
The YCB small marker is the focus item.
The rack provides the display position and neighboring-tool constraints.
The marker starts in the writing-tool rack.
The label starts facing away so reorientation is observable.
The marker must be reachable without dislodging neighboring tools.
The rack must have sufficient clearance for rotation and release.
The robot must grasp and rotate the marker.
Label orientation, rack containment, and neighbor stability require inspection.
The proposed activity is household writing-tool organization.

success_criteria: The small marker label faces outward while the marker remains fully supported in the writing_tool_rack.
Adjacent writing tools remain in their original slots and the small marker is stable after release.
setup: Place the capped small marker label-back in the rack with two neighboring writing tools and enough clearance to rotate it.
Use a non-slip rack on a level bench and mark the desired outward-facing orientation.
reset: Rotate the small marker back to label-back without moving its neighbors.
Restore the original slot occupancy and confirm the rack remains stable.
quality_checks: Check the label-front orientation from the designated viewing direction.
Check for neighbor displacement, marker tip exposure, and any marker or rack instability.
failure_modes: Marker remains label-back or is placed outside its rack slot.
Neighboring tools are knocked out of alignment.
Marker rolls, tips, or exposes its writing tip.

requirements.reason: The workshop provides a fastening-tool rack and stable bench.
The YCB adjustable wrench is the focus tool.
Related fastening tools define the organization group.
The rack is the marked destination for the wrench.
The wrench starts on the bench.
The grouping goal requires other fastening tools.
The rack must support the wrench without tipping.
The robot must move the rigid wrench into the rack.
Group membership, jaw accessibility, and rack stability require inspection.
The proposed activity is household tool organization.

success_criteria: The adjustable wrench is supported in the fastening_tool_rack with the other fastening tools.
Its adjustable jaw remains accessible and the organized group is stable after release.
setup: Place the wrench and at least two fastening tools on the bench beside a stable rack with a dedicated wrench position.
Set the wrench to a neutral jaw opening and keep the rack free of sharp or powered tools during the trial.
reset: Remove the wrench from the rack and return it to the marked bench position.
Restore the related fastening tools and neutral jaw opening without changing the rack.
quality_checks: Verify the wrench is grouped with fastening tools rather than mixed into an unrelated storage slot.
Check that the wrench can be retrieved without moving another tool and that the rack did not shift.
failure_modes: Wrench placed in the wrong rack or outside the organization area.
Jaw or handle blocks access to neighboring tools.
Rack tips or the wrench is left unstable.

requirements.reason: The workshop contains a marked handle-first handover zone.
The YCB Phillips screwdriver is the item being transferred.
A consenting recipient is required.
The screwdriver starts on the workbench.
The screwdriver must be reachable with its tip path controlled.

The robot must grasp and orient the screwdriver.
The goal requires a controlled transfer to a person.

success_criteria: The worker has a stable grasp on the Phillips screwdriver handle before robot release.

Record any tip exposure, tip contact, drop, or collision with another tool.

quality_checks: Inspect that the full tool, including its tip, is contained in the intended tray position.
Check for exposed-tip contact, tray displacement, rolling, or interference with neighboring tools.
